seoTitle: Time Zone Converter - Convert Time Between Cities
metaDescription: Easily convert time between different time zones. Find out the exact time difference and smoothly coordinate schedules across the world.
intro: Trying to figure out what 9:00 AM in Tokyo means for your morning schedule in London? Coordinating across global time zones can be a mathematical headache, especially when Daylight Saving Time rules differ from country to country. Our free online Time Zone Converter takes the guesswork out of international scheduling by letting you instantly translate any specific date and time from one time zone into another. Whether you are organizing a multinational conference call, booking a flight, or setting a deadline for a remote team, this tool provides pinpoint accuracy. It completely eliminates the risk of miscommunication caused by time zone confusion, ensuring everyone shows up exactly when they are supposed to.
whatIs: The Time Zone Converter is a precision utility that translates a specific date and time between any two global time zones or cities. Unlike a world clock that only shows the current live time, a time zone converter allows you to project forward or backward into the calendar to determine what a specific future or past moment looks like in a different part of the world. It relies on the comprehensive IANA Time Zone Database (Olson database), which contains the historical and current time zone rules for every region on Earth. This means the converter automatically accounts for complex anomalies like Daylight Saving Time transitions, regional offset changes, and hemisphere differences without you needing to do any manual math.
howToUse: Select your starting timezone from the first dropdown menu.
Enter the specific date and time you want to convert.
Select your target timezone from the second dropdown menu.
The tool will instantly display the converted time and the hour difference.
howItWorks: When you select a starting date and time, a source time zone, and a destination time zone, the converter performs a two-step calculation. First, it translates your input time into Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) based on the exact offset rules that apply to the source location on that specific calendar date. Second, it takes that UTC moment and applies the offset rules for the destination location on the same exact date. This dual-conversion approach ensures absolute accuracy even if one location observes Daylight Saving Time and the other does not, or if the two locations transition into DST on entirely different dates. The calculation happens instantly in your browser.
workedExample: Imagine you live in San Francisco (PST/PDT) and you need to schedule a virtual meeting for March 15th at 10:00 AM local time. You want to know what time your colleague in Sydney, Australia (AEST/AEDT) needs to join. You enter 'March 15, 10:00 AM', select 'San Francisco' as the source, and 'Sydney' as the destination. The converter calculates the difference and displays the result: 'March 16, 4:00 AM in Sydney'. Notice that not only is the hour completely different, but the meeting actually falls on the next calendar day for your colleague. Armed with this accurate information, you might decide to shift the meeting to a time that is more reasonable for both parties.
resultInterpretation: The result clearly displays the converted date and time in your selected destination zone. It is crucial to pay attention to both the time and the date, as large time zone gaps frequently push events across the international date line or past midnight into a different calendar day. The tool also typically indicates the exact UTC offset for both the source and destination at that specific moment in time (e.g., UTC-7 vs UTC+11). If you are scheduling a recurring event, remember that the time difference between the two locations might change later in the year when one or both regions enter or exit Daylight Saving Time.
useCases: Scheduling Interviews: Ensuring you and an international candidate log on at the exact same moment.
Flight Connections: Understanding exactly how much layover time you have when crossing zones.
Remote Collaboration: Setting deadlines that are perfectly synced for team members in different countries.
tipsAndLimitations: Be careful around the months of March and October/November, as Daylight Saving Time shifts can change the hour difference between two cities.
You can quickly click the 'Swap' button in the middle to reverse the conversion.

faq.question: Does it automatically handle Daylight Saving Time?
faq.answer: Yes. Because the converter checks the specific date you enter, it accurately applies the correct Daylight Saving Time rules for that exact day in both locations.

faq.question: What does UTC mean?
faq.answer: UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time. It is the primary time standard by which the world regulates clocks and time, effectively replacing GMT.

disclaimer: This tool relies on your browser's internal timezone database; ensure your system is updated for the most accurate Daylight Saving boundaries.
